setlist.title: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (4 reviews): Reviewer's favorite Jack Straw, with notable interplay between Jerry and Phil from the opening notes; Reviewer calls the Jack Straw beautiful [12][13][15][18]
- **Deep Elem Blues** (4 reviews): Described as very tight; Very good, by the standards of Deep Elem renditions [14][18][20][23]
- **Touch Of Grey** (3 reviews): Reviewer finds it feels different as the second set opener; Reviewer hears it as an early, proto version of the later song [12][14][15]
- **My Brother Esau** (2 reviews): Reviewer felt the band was searching for a good Esau, waiting for the jam; Great percussion that the audience recording's quality brings out [20][22]
- **Deal** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out Deal as amazing, and says the second set repays many listens; Counted among the better Deals from this period, after strong Jerry playing in the first set [13][21]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Jerry plays fantastic licks [22]
- **It's All Over Now Baby Blue** (1 other source): Encore contains a tease more like Wang Dang Doodle [5]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Reviewer says Jerry flubs this song [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-08-27.aud.herbst.31635.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 19 songs; 143 min; rated 2.75/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd83-08-27.sennheiser.dodd.12359.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 17 songs; 143 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound quality of this Sennheiser audience tape is extremely crisp [21]
- **gd1983-08-27.aud.keith.92307.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 17 songs; 140 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd83-08-27.aud.hinko.16439.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 17 songs; 141 min; rated 4.17/5 by 18 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience tape where the instruments sound clearly human-driven and natural [15]

## Around the show

- Uploader guesses the taping spot was front-of-board on Jerry's side, about halfway back on the floor [1]
- Taper was in a group of about 25 people set up front-of-board [3]
- Reviewer considers the rest of the show mostly standard 1980s fare, apart from Jack Straw and maybe Deal [18]
- First set judged outstanding throughout; second set good but not great [21]
- Pre-drums part of set two is tasty apart from lyrical flubs; set one is solid [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-08-27.aud.herbst.31635.flac16**: taped by Jamie Herbst; source: unknown mics > Sony D5 cassette deck (probable) [1]. Also: Uploader says tracks d1t08 and d1t10 are each missing their first few seconds [1]
- **gd83-08-27.sennheiser.dodd.12359.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD(Senn. 421Âs)>MC>DAT>CDREac >shn (secure with proper offsets) by Ernie Dodd [2]. Also: Transferred from the Sennheiser audience tape by Ernie Dodd, with missing tracks later supplied on disc 3 [2]
- **gd1983-08-27.aud.keith.92307.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Keith; transferred by Andrew F.; source: FOB, Nakamichi CM300's > Sony TC-D5 (MAC) > C1 (Sony TC-D5 > Marantz PMD-340 > TDK SA-90's) (no Dolby) [3]. Also: Taper patched from another's deck with bad batteries, so his tape sounded fuzzy; he dubbed a nearby taper's copy over his master; Source is Keith's copy, with patches from ShnID-16439 in Jack Straw and Space; Little Red Rooster cuts in after tape flip [3]
- **gd83-08-27.aud.hinko.16439.sbeok.shnf**: Audience source lineage: NAK 700 to Sony D-5 to MC to HHB CD writer [12]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Concertposterauction.com: [Grateful Dead Seattle Center Coliseum 1983 Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/213534/Grateful-Dead-Seattle-Center-Coliseum-1983-Concert-Poster) [25]
- Poster by Kathleen Elizabeth Fowler Grateful: [1983-08-27 Seattle Center Coliseum, Seattle, WA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1983-08-27-seattle-center-coliseum-seattle-wa-usa/) [26]
